papers.paper: SOSD: Marcus et al., Benchmarking Learned Indexes (VLDB 2020), learnedsystems/SOSD @ f52f4cb
papers.warmup: VERIFIED. There is no explicit warm-up. Build is followed directly by the lookup loop. The paper calls its main setting 'warm-cache, tight-loop' (p.1). With -r R>1, the R passes run back to back on the same built index, so pass 1 includes the cold start. Default R=1 (benchmark.cc L112-113). execute.sh defaults num_iterations=1 and passes it as -r; reproduce.sh calls execute.sh without -n. Nuance the researcher missed: build itself touches the whole data array and index just before the loop. With --pareto, many configurations of each index run one after another in one process over the same data_ array and lookup vector, so only the first configuration sees a cold data array.
papers.timed_ops: VERIFIED. 10M lookups per dataset (paper Sec. 3 'For each dataset, we generate 10M random lookup keys', local sosd_paper.txt L787). generate.cc: FastRandom(42), positive lookups drawn uniformly from unique keys, with a retry cap on heavily duplicated keys; negative lookups only if a ratio argument is given (prepare.sh gives none). The timer is high_resolution_clock via util::timing around the whole loop: EqualityLookup, std::lower_bound last mile, payload sum and result check.
papers.repetitions_and_aggregate: VERIFIED. R passes in one process with one build (benchmark.h L193-225). The CSV output gives the median of the per-pass mean ns/lookup (benchmark.h L389-403). The paper does not state R; the published pipeline uses R=1.
papers.other_steady_state_measures: VERIFIED. util::set_cpu_affinity(0) pins the main thread to core 0 (benchmark.cc L179-180). --cold-cache sums a 26e6/8-element uint64 buffer (26 MB, the hard-coded L3 size) before every lookup, then _mm_mfence, then times each lookup individually; the result check is inside the timer (benchmark.h L91-92, L239-264). Paper Sec. 4.4.1 / Fig. 14: the warm-cache gain is 2x to 2.5x for all five structures. --fence adds __sync_synchronize between lookups. No huge-page or prefault handling.
papers.source: Paper arXiv 2006.12804 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.12804) p.1, Sec. 3, Sec. 4.4.1 (local sosd_paper.txt L99-100, L787, L1478-1497). Code https://github.com/learnedsystems/SOSD/blob/f52f4cba01dfcd37f1574551fccef00198863b88/benchmark.h; the local copy is byte-identical to that commit (checked by diff).

papers.paper: NFL: Wu et al. (VLDB 2022), luffy06/NFL @ fe71172
papers.warmup: VERIFIED. There is none. Each repetition is a separate process (benchmark.sh calls the binary once per repeat). papers.paper: GRE: Wongkham et al., Are Updatable Learned Indexes Ready? (VLDB 2022), gre4index/GRE @ e807edc
papers.warmup: VERIFIED. There is none. run_benchmark() calls load_keys(), then generate_operations() (BEFORE bulk load), then prepare() (bulk load), then run(). In run(), TSCNS init busy-spins about 10 ms to calibrate, then start_time=rdtsc() after an omp barrier. Local patch (verified in scratchpad/gre_wf/GRE benchmark.h L318-345 and gre_lite_patch.h): --warmup_num=W untimed index->get() calls on the calling thread; --pin_core applied before the warm-up loop. The warm-up keys are generated before pinning, so with OMP_NUM_THREADS>1 that generation runs multi-threaded.
papers.timed_ops: CORRECTED. Paper read-only: 'Bulk load all the 200M keys and randomly lookup for 800M keys' (with replacement in code). Code default operations_num=1e9, init_table_ratio default 0.5, so read-only needs --init_table_ratio=1. The lookup sampler is NOT 'mt19937 seed 1866'. get_search_keys runs inside '#pragma omp parallel' with the DEFAULT OpenMP team: each thread uses mt19937_64 seeded (seed + omp_thread_id) and fills a static 'omp for' chunk with uniform_int_distribution<int> over init_keys. std::mt19937(seed=1866) is used only for the key shuffle and for op-type draws. Consequence: GRE's lookup trace depends on OMP_NUM_THREADS / core count at generation time, not only on --seed. The timed loop is rdtsc around an 'omp for schedule(dynamic,10000)' over a pre-generated array of (op, key) pairs, 16 B each.
papers.repetitions_and_aggregate: VERIFIED. 'For each workload and index, we repeat the experiment three times and report the average throughput ... and the average latency after bulk loading.' The seed is fixed by default, so repeats differ only in noise. run_benchmark loops over all --index and --thread_num values in one process, so one invocation can hold several runs on the same ops array.
papers.other_steady_state_measures: CORRECTED. The code has no pinning, but the paper DOES pin in one experiment: for the tail-latency study, XIndex's operational and background threads were pinned to the same core (gre_paper.txt L1324-1327). Hyper-threading is disabled by default. The Interleave NUMA policy is used for the 1-4 socket scaling study. No huge-page or prefault handling; bulk load writes the index and generation writes the ops array, so both are resident. Optional --latency_sample: 1% rdtsc sampling inside the timed loop.
papers.source: arXiv 2207.02900 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02900) Sec. 3.3-3.4, 4 (local gre_paper.txt L562-582, L630-634, L908-913, L1324-1331); code https://github.com/gre4index/GRE/blob/e807edcef51df6732f07f94d4c797fb3897519ba/src/benchmark/benchmark.h L130-140, L236-290, L297-391, L555-566 and src/benchmark/utils.h L197-214 (local unpatched copy identical to the commit); src/tscns.h L53-57.

recommendation:
VERIFICATION SUMMARY. The local code copies of SOSD, PGM, RS, ALEX, NFL, GRE, CARMI and TLI are byte-identical to the cited commits (checked by diff against raw.githubusercontent). The researcher's table is mostly accurate. Corrections:
(a) RMI. 'Randomly selected' is from Sec. 2.3 (TF prototype). Sec. 3.7 does not describe its lookup keys at all.
(b) PGM and RS. The repo benchmarks postdate the papers (PGM benchmark.hpp first committed 2021-03-22; RS bench.cc 2020-06-30). RS's paper numbers come from SOSD. Both repo drivers run several indexes or configurations one after another in one process, which gives later ones a warm data array.
(c) RS. The citation is p.3, not p.2.
(d) NFL. The timed loop is at L221-258 (run_lipp); L136-206 is the dispatcher. The unused 'uniform' mode reseeds every batch, so it repeats the same 256 keys.
(e) CSV. The paper says 'repeating the query 25 times', not 'back to back'. Its harness is based on Bachfischer et al. 2022 (arXiv 2207.11575), whose protocol is unverified.
(f) GRE. The lookup sampler is mt19937_64 seeded (seed + OpenMP thread id) inside an omp parallel region of DEFAULT size; mt19937(1866) is only for the shuffle and op types. GRE's trace therefore depends on OMP_NUM_THREADS. The GRE paper does pin (XIndex threads, in the latency study).
(g) The headline 'Only SOSD pins' is wrong. AIDB pins its worker thread, and GRE pins in one experiment. SOSD is the only one whose public harness pins by default.
The 10-of-12 count (no separate stream warm-up) stands. AIDB is the only one with an explicit warm-up: 20M untimed, then 100M timed, pinned, huge pages disabled.

CORRECTED PROTOCOL for the new read-only index in patched GRE (single thread, 200M keys, 100M uniform lookups):

(1) Warm-up size. Keep W = 20,000,000.
- Flags: --warmup_num=20000000 --init_table_ratio=1.0 --operations_num=100000000 --read=1.0 --insert=0 --thread_num=1.
- This matches AIDB and is 53x the at-most-375k cold transient measured on the Mac (PROTOCOL.md 3.2). That figure must be re-measured on the x86 server (step 7).
- Bias arithmetic stands: 0.4M ops x 20% / 100M = 0.08%.
- Cost: about 20% more lookup time and a 160 MB transient key buffer, freed before the timed region.

(2) Distribution, seed and OMP_NUM_THREADS. This is a NEW MANDATORY item the researcher omitted.
- Run with OMP_NUM_THREADS=1. GRE's sampler seeds one generator per OpenMP thread (seed + tid). With T>1 threads, the warm-up stream (seed+1, thread 0) is identical to the first W/T draws of the timed stream's thread-1 chunk. About (T-1)/T of the warm-up would then replay exact timed keys, so the researcher's claim 'without replaying the exact timed trace' holds only at T=1. gre_lite.sh L56-57 already documents this.
- Keep seed 1866 for the timed stream and seed+1 for the warm-up, with the same distribution (uniform, or scrambled Zipf if the timed run is Zipf). The Zipf hot set is the same, which is intended.
- State honestly that with OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 the timed trace matches GRE's in distribution, not key for key. GRE-as-published traces depend on the generating machine's OMP team size. AIDB's harness is unpublished, so comparability with it is also only distributional.
- No sequential or strided warm-up.

(3) Pinning and NUMA. Unchanged in substance.
- Use --pin_core on an isolated non-zero core.
- The patch pins only inside run(), after load, generation and bulk load. So wrap the whole process: numactl --cpunodebind=N --membind=N with a core on node N.
- With thread_num=1 the omp parallel team is the master thread, so the warm-up and the timed loop run on the same pinned thread (verified in code).
- Set the performance governor, turn turbo off, check cpu-migrations=0, keep the machine idle.
- Note: TSCNS init busy-spins about 10 ms between the warm-up and the timed region. This is harmless; there is no sleep.

(4) Huge pages and prefault.
- Primary arm with THP=never, recording /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/{enabled,defrag}. AIDB's 'Hugepages are disabled' does not say whether it means THP or hugetlbfs, so state our interpretation.
- An optional THP=always sensitivity arm must cover all indexes.
- No prefault in GRE: the index and the ops array are written before the timed region.
- Correct the wording 'no prefault effect'. Our idle replication found the effect not significant at n=6 (Mann-Whitney U=8, critical value 5), but the first-1/16 medians were -14.4% without prefault vs -3.7% with it. Minor faults were identical (1,104,188 vs 1,104,194), so the transient is not paging. Say 'no detectable paging effect', not 'no effect'.

(5) Cold vs warm reporting.
- Headline: the warm 100M-lookup throughput.
- The GRE-as-published comparison arm (W=0, same seed and same OMP_NUM_THREADS=1) is the right cold-inclusive number.
- Demote warmup_ns/W to an informal indicator. It is a different loop: steady_clock, a plain key array, no (op, key) pair stream, no op-type dispatch, no omp dynamic scheduling. It is not directly comparable to GRE's timed throughput.
- No SOSD-style per-lookup flush as a primary metric (2x-2.5x regime change, SOSD Fig. 14).

(6) Repetitions. Unchanged.
- At least 3, preferably 5, separate processes per (index, dataset), with one index per process (gre_lite.sh: the indexInterface has no virtual destructor). Interleave indexes round-robin.
- Report the arithmetic mean (as GRE, NFL and LIPP do), plus the median and min-max or a 95% CI, and ratios against baselines measured in the same rounds.

(7) Validity check. REDESIGNED: the researcher's criterion cannot be tested.
- The researcher proposed accepting W=20M if W=0 differs by less than about 0.5%, using 3 repetitions. With per-process sigma about 6% (PROTOCOL.md 3.2, Mac), the SE of a 3-vs-3 difference is about 5%. A 0.5% gap can neither be confirmed nor excluded, and the predicted bias (about 0.1%) is far below detectability.
- Instead, measure the transient within each process. On 2 datasets (fb, osm), for the new index and LIPP, run W in {0, 1M, 20M} x 3 processes with GRE's own --latency_sample (1% rdtsc sampling).
- Bin the sampled latencies into, for example, 1M-op chunks of the timed region, and compare chunk 1 with the median chunk inside the same process. This is paired, so per-process noise cancels.
